# About me

I'm a chemical engineering student at the University of Delaware, originally from Reading, Pennsylvania. I work with Arthi Jayaraman's lab on computational studies of block-copolymer structures, and I'm an R&D co-op with DuPont Water Solutions, where I work on ion-exchange resin synthesis and applications.

## Interests

I'm interested in polymer science, statistics, data science, and signal processing, especially where they overlap. I plan to pursue a PhD in chemical engineering focused on polymer physics and machine learning.

## Current work

At DuPont, I work on the synthesis and application of ion-exchange resins. In the Jayaraman Lab, I use molecular simulation and analysis to study block-copolymer structures. My personal projects are usually small scientific tools, data analyses, or experiments in making technical work easier to inspect and reuse.

## Background

I like work that connects physical intuition with computation. That might mean writing a browser tool for lab data, building a constrained optimization pipeline, or using simulation to ask a question about a material.

For a fuller record of my experience, [download my CV](CV.pdf). You can also reach me at [kwode@udel.edu](mailto:kwode@udel.edu).
